# Question answer: generator shortcuts

## Strongest canonical-fit rival

The strongest plausible shortcut is **“find the unmatched dihedral shape class, then return its whole tight crop”** (`whole_singleton`) instead of extracting its boundary. It uses the difficult part of the intended rule and differs in only one operation, so it is more plausible than a purely positional guess. It fits every canonical demonstration because every canonical singleton has no interior cell: whole crop and boundary crop are identical there.

A second independent canonical-fit rival is **“return the boundary of the last motif in scan order”** (`last_motif_boundary`). It also fits every canonical pair because the canonical singleton happens to be last.

## How it was checked

I generated the input through the final `3.0.0` source, verified `self_check(input) == []`, and ran the supported canonical authority command. The retained report is `checks/49197-counterexample-racket.json`; it records generator SHA-256 `a23b045bf7c4c3f8bb72e8aaf5eb7662f156e835d24711308ad6b25422b41dcd`, matching rule hash `4303be5db475`, and a valid Racket output. The machine-readable input, both rival outputs, seed, overrides, hashes, and command are in `repo/generators/49197f3c9375/counterexamples/strongest-rivals.json`, and a source-bound regression replays it.

## Does the proposed generator emit such cases?

**Yes.** Interior-bearing singleton roles directly refute `whole_singleton`, and first/middle singleton roles refute `last_motif_boundary`. The six-role schedule alternates boundary-only/interior-bearing targets while cycling first/middle/last positions. The focused regression exhausts all 24 cyclic starts in every difficulty band and every one-pair query holdout; the larger Racket census materialized 300 lessons (1,200 unique inputs and 1,200 rotations) with zero surviving declared-rival ambiguity.
